title: Impedance mapping release lane and heat budget notes — Feb 2026 (draft)
content:
Purpose
---
Working notes for an alternative way to think about staged launches: treat each lane as an impedance surface (how much heat it allows) and budget requesters (features/traffic cohorts) against that heat budget. Goal is to reduce surprise surge/latency regressions and make rollback decisions more deterministic.

Status
---
Draft — still need: perf bench for seq-len 512 on A100-80GB (ticket JIRA-RELEASE-3456), SRE to sign off on throttle curves, product to confirm feature gating buckets.

High-level approach (short)
---
- Map the set of release lanes to three impedance classes: low, medium, high.
- Assign each feature/variant a heat cost (tokens/sec * expected concurrency * ops complexity factor).
- Define lane heat budgets per region + model variant.
- Route cohorts by user-level tags to lanes.
- Enforce budget via token-throttles + queue-length limits + circuit-breaker shortcircuit.

Impedance classes (proposal)
---
1) Low impedance (fastpath): critical infra + high-latency-sensitive customer routes. Budget: 0.6 x baseline capacity. Throttle: soft at 75% prefixed tokens/s, hard at 95% prefixed tokens/s.
2) Medium impedance (default): normal requests + PLG experimental variants. Budget: 0.4 x baseline capacity. Throttle: soft 60%, hard 90%.
3) High impedance (background): batch jobs, heavy evals, training-inference offline. Budget: 0.1 x baseline spare. Throttle: soft 40%, hard 80%.

Heat budget calc (example)
---
- Baseline capacity (region us-west-2, model: redwood-medium-7B q4f16) = 100k tokens/s aggregated across pool.
- Low lane budget = 60k tks/s, medium = 40k tks/s, high = 10k tks/s (note: high + medium > baseline, must reconcile via burst policy).
- Feature A estimate: 0.5 tks/req * 100 rps = 50 tks/s -> heat cost = 50.
- Feature B (chat-heavy): 4 tks/req * 25 rps = 100 tks/s -> heat cost = 100 (assign to medium or high depending on risk).

Rollout calendar (compact)
---
- Day -3 (2026-02-08): Release branch cut, smoke test matrix run on staging; perf bench for seq 512 (bench owner: Marco).
- Day -1 (2026-02-10): Canary lane deploy (low impedance), 2% of traffic for 3 hours; smoke tests (latency p50/p95), error rate < 0.1% target.
- Day 0 (2026-02-11): Ramp to 10% over 4 hours if gates pass. Telemetry bakeoff window 2 hours at 10%.
- Day +1 (2026-02-12): Ramp to 35% over 6 hours. Run synthetic workload with worst-case prefix to validate KV cache behavior.
- Day +2 (2026-02-13): Evaluate metrics and stakeholder signoff; optional warm-up to 60% if stable.
- Day +3 (2026-02-14): Full roll to medium lane or continue gradual ramp depending on heat consumption.

Throttle curves and decision points (quick)
---
- Soft throttle triggers: token budget exceed for 3 consecutive 1-min buckets OR p95 latency > SLO by 20% for 5 minutes.
- Hard throttle / rollback triggers: error rate above 0.5% sustained for 5 mins OR p99 latency > 2x SLO for 3 mins. Immediate rollback to last good model-version.
- Auto-fallback: route 30% of traffic to the last stable variant when soft throttle occurs; escalate if soft triggers persist > 15 mins.

Smoke test checklist (staging + canary)
---
- Basic generation end-to-end: simple prompt -> validate tokenization and output size.
- P95 latency < 160ms (fastpath), p95 < 400ms (medium) — region-coded.
- KV-cache behavior: repeated prefix -> verify p95 drops by >= 30% vs cold.
- Memory leaks: 2h soak on instance for background tasks.
- Auth/logging: check token-level logging preserved, no PII leak in sample outputs (QA spot-check).
- Rate-limit behavior: simulate burst x5 baseline; observe queueing and throttles.

Telemetry gating (metrics to watch)
---
- Request success rate (4xx/5xx breakdown) by route and lane.
- Latency histograms (p50/p90/p95/p99) by model-version.
- CPU/GPU utilization per node pool, IO/PCIe stall rate.
- Token emission rate and dropped token count.
- Cache hit ratio (KV prefix) and cold start ratio.
- Error signatures: OOM, CUDA kernel failures, out-of-memory swaps, internal rate-limit rejects.

Rollback plan (short)
---
- If hard triggers -> immediate rollback to previous model-variant using rollout controller quick-path.
- Post-rollback: preserve 10% of traffic on failed variant for postmortem capture, if safe.
- Postmortem owner: Devon Brooks. Timeline: 24h preliminary, 72h full report.

Communication snippets (for Slack / status page)
---
- Pre-launch: "@here Starting canary for 'release/2026-02-11' (low-lane). Expected 2% traffic for 3h. Watch #release-ops and SLO board. Contact: @Aisha."
- On soft throttle: "Notice: soft throttle on low-lane; auto-fallback to stable variant 30% engaged. Observed p95 latency rise; investigating. (ops)"
- On rollback: "ROLLED BACK: release/2026-02-11 -> previous-stable. Root cause under investigation; see JIRA-RELEASE-3456."

Release notes (user-facing draft)
---
Title: Faster generation for short prompts (Feb 2026)
Summary: This rollout includes inference engine optimizations that reduce latency for short prompts and improves cache efficiency for conversational workloads. No API changes.
What's new: Reduced median latency for short prompts (<=64 tokens) by ~15% in our hosted API; improved stability under bursty traffic.
Known limitations: Heavy long-sequence workloads (seq >512) may still see variable latencies; customers on dedicated pools should test with their traces.
Migration notes: None. If you depend on deterministic p99 latency, please pin to stable model-variant until we complete the ramp.

Open questions / TODOs
---
- Confirm exact baseline capacity numbers with infra (Marco) — actioned but awaiting final numbers.
- Finalize lane tagging for client cohorts (Product/Ruth).
- Add automated smoke-run triggers in the console for every canary deployment (needs ticket).

Appendix — quick links
---
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/1428
- Jira: JIRA-RELEASE-3456 (bench + telemetry work)
- Confluence draft (gates): confluence:release-gates-telemetry

Notes to self
---
- Keep heat budgets conservative for first two rollouts.
- If cache-hit amplification appears (cache makes latencies worse at medium load), pause and open narrow rollback.
- Remember to capture sample payloads for any p99 spike (store in secure bucket)
